title: PCSK9 loss-of-function variants: human-genetic positive control for strong effect and target plausibility
summary: Positive-control record for MKH-PAT-0015. PCSK9 loss-of-function is encoded as a human-genetic case where sequence variation had large, interpretable phenotype and disease-risk associations, preventing the pattern from becoming anti-candidate or anti-human-genetics.

status_history.note: Promoted as a strong-effect human-genetics counterweight to psychiatric candidate-gene nulls.

place.scope: ARIC/NEJM abstracted evidence; therapy-development history not yet encoded

claims.claim: Cohen et al. examined sequence variants in PCSK9 associated with reduced plasma LDL cholesterol and compared 15-year coronary-heart-disease incidence in the ARIC study according to variant presence or absence.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: The PubMed abstract reports that PCSK9 nonsense mutations in Black subjects were associated with a 28% LDL-cholesterol reduction and an 88% CHD-risk reduction, while PCSK9 sequence variation in White subjects was associated with a 15% LDL reduction and a 47% CHD-risk reduction.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: As a control record, PCSK9 shows that MKH-PAT-0015 must distinguish weak, diffuse, underpowered candidate-gene literatures from strong-effect human-genetic relations with interpretable biology; it does not by itself encode the later drug-development, clinical-outcome, or safety history of PCSK9 inhibitors.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

evidence_refs.support_type: control role and limits encoded in this record

evidence_profile.why_control_not_case: It is not a failed association; it calibrates the pattern around effect size, phenotype tightness, and human-genetic target plausibility.

type_payload.fit_rationale: Strong-effect, biologically interpretable human-genetic relation that prevents overgeneralizing from psychiatric candidate-gene failures.
